source: Inspired by assets/ground_truth/internal_inbox/designer_reference_slides.pptx slide 14 (S14 — 'Our proposition for Globe Telecom'). The original is a denser 4-row × 3-column matrix with row labels and column headers; our flat cards schema cannot express the 2D structure directly, so this example flattens to 6 representative capability cells. A 2D variant would require schema extension (row_labels, column_labels).
intent: Show six (or fewer fillable) parallel capabilities, components, or scope areas as a structured matrix when ordering does not imply sequence. Use for capability matrices, component overviews, scope grids — not for processes or comparisons.
invariants: exactly 6 cells laid out as a 2-row × 3-column grid
each cell has a top accent bar (xs height) in a distinct theme color
cell title uses subtitle type style, bold, text_primary
cell body uses body type style, text_secondary
card has bg_primary fill with subtle accent_6 border
header bar with kicker + claim-headline sits above the matrix
no metrics, no images, no bullets — pure title+body cells
variables: number of cells (4-6, padded to fill 2x2, 2x3 or 3x2 grids evenly)
cell body length (12-25 words, single-sentence prose)
header kicker label and headline phrasing
